"""
@ingroup PATTERN_API
@brief Pack the UV islands of the non-fabric objects attached to the given patterns into the target UV tile —
the companion of MovePatternsToUVSpace for hardware: buttons sitting on the patterns, the zipper
tape(s) stitched to them, the zipper hardware (obj teeth/slider/puller/stoppers), and the trims
(buckles, rings, beads, ...) glued to them. Note that button, zipper-hardware and trim islands are
STYLE-level in the UV editor (one island per style, shared by every instance of that style) — moving
them also affects other garments using the same style. Graphics/prints are not handled here because
they follow their pattern's island automatically. Islands are deduplicated across the call.
The objects are placed in the FREE part of the target tile: whatever is already in that tile and is not
being moved (in practice the garment's pattern islands, put there by an earlier MovePatternsToUVSpace
call) is measured first, the largest strip left over around it is chosen, and the nested objects are
shrunk to fit that strip. So calling MovePatternsToUVSpace and then this function on the same tile
does not make the objects land on top of the patterns.
@return JSON: {"status","movedIslands","fitScale","freeBand":{"x","y","width","height"},"bbox",
"results":[{"patternIndex","ok","objectIslands","message"}],"message"}. "objectIslands" is the number
of attached-object islands contributed by that pattern (0 with ok=true means its objects were already
packed via an earlier pattern in the same call). "fitScale" is the extra shrink applied to make the
objects fit the free band (1 = none). On failure: {"status":"failed","message"}.
@param _componentTypes: which object types to move — any of "button", "zipper", "trim". Empty (default) moves
every type. Pass a single type to give e.g. all zippers one tile and all buttons another.
"""
